ptr.note: sd is the caller's AVFrameSideData ** variable (never NULL); *sd is NULL with *nb_sd == 0, or an av_realloc_array'd block of *nb_sd pointers to distinct entries, each av_mallocz'd by add_side_data_from_buf_ext and owning its buf reference and metadata dictionary. Builds an entry into the array around *pbuf: with UNIQUE it first removes every entry of the type (even if the addition then fails); for a type without MULTI an existing entry is replaced in place only with REPLACE (old buf unref'd, metadata freed, buf and its window stored), else C returns NULL; otherwise a new av_mallocz'd entry holding buf and its window is appended. Rust: frame.rs::SideDataArrayMut::add / SideDataArray::add (buffer-frame wave 2 batch 0), no NEW_REF.
The caller's entry count, read and written with the array (an int, never NULL); C keeps it equal to the number of entry pointers in *sd.

The caller's AVBufferRef * slot (never NULL; *pbuf must be non-NULL: the REPLACE path reads buf->data unchecked). Without NEW_REF the entry takes *pbuf over on success and C NULLs the slot; on failure the slot keeps the caller's reference. With NEW_REF C takes its own av_buffer_ref (failure returns NULL), unrefs it again when it adds nothing, and never writes the slot.

The new or replaced entry, owned by the array, NULL when C added nothing (non-MULTI type present without REPLACE, ENOMEM, NEW_REF's av_buffer_ref failing). Its payload is the window of the buffer it took, initialised as the caller's buffer was.

sd is the caller's AVFrameSideData ** variable (never NULL); *sd is NULL with *nb_sd == 0, or an av_realloc_array'd block of *nb_sd pointers to distinct entries, each av_mallocz'd by add_side_data_from_buf_ext and owning its buf reference and metadata dictionary. Receives the copy (EINVAL when sd or nb_sd is NULL, or *nb_sd > 0 with a NULL *sd): with UNIQUE C first removes every entry of src's type; for a type without MULTI an existing entry gets src's buffer (av_buffer_replace), data/size and a copy of its metadata only with REPLACE, else EEXIST; otherwise a new entry is appended holding av_buffer_ref(src->buf), src's data/size and av_dict_copy of its metadata (removed again if that copy fails).
The caller's entry count, read and written with the array (an int, never NULL); C keeps it equal to the number of entry pointers in *sd.

The source entry, read only (NULL gives EINVAL). Its buf must be non-NULL (av_buffer_ref/av_buffer_replace dereference it). The copy is a new entry (or the replaced one) sharing src's buffer by count, so neither payload is writable while both live, and holding its own deep copy of the metadata.

sd is the caller's AVFrameSideData ** variable (never NULL); *sd is NULL with *nb_sd == 0, or an av_realloc_array'd block of *nb_sd pointers to distinct entries, each av_mallocz'd by add_side_data_from_buf_ext and owning its buf reference and metadata dictionary. Consumes the whole array: free_side_data_entry on every entry (av_buffer_unref(&buf), av_dict_free(&metadata), av_freep(entry)), then *nb_sd = 0 and av_freep(sd), which NULLs *sd. Rust: Drop for frame.rs::SideDataArray (buffer-frame wave 2 batch 0).
The caller's entry count, read and written with the array (an int, never NULL); C keeps it equal to the number of entry pointers in *sd.

sd is the caller's AVFrameSideData ** variable (never NULL); *sd is NULL with *nb_sd == 0, or an av_realloc_array'd block of *nb_sd pointers to distinct entries, each av_mallocz'd by add_side_data_from_buf_ext and owning its buf reference and metadata dictionary. Builds an entry into the array: with UNIQUE it first removes every entry of the type; for a type without MULTI an existing entry is replaced in place only with REPLACE (old buf unref'd, metadata freed, the new av_buffer_alloc'd buffer's window stored) and otherwise C returns NULL; else the block grows by av_realloc_array and a new av_mallocz'd entry is appended. On failure the fresh buffer is unref'd; the block may already have grown. C defect (OOM only): when av_buffer_alloc fails and REPLACE meets an existing non-MULTI entry, replace_side_data_from_buf dereferences the NULL buf (buf->data); a wrapper must not reach C's REPLACE path without a buffer.
The caller's entry count, read and written with the array (an int, never NULL); C keeps it equal to the number of entry pointers in *sd.

The new or replaced entry, owned by the array (the caller must not free it), NULL on failure or when a non-MULTI entry exists and REPLACE is unset. Its payload is an av_buffer_alloc'd window of size bytes, UNINITIALISED: the caller writes it in place.

sd is the caller's AVFrameSideData ** variable (never NULL); *sd is NULL with *nb_sd == 0, or an av_realloc_array'd block of *nb_sd pointers to distinct entries, each av_mallocz'd by add_side_data_from_buf_ext and owning its buf reference and metadata dictionary. Drops every entry whose type equals the argument (free_side_data_entry, then the last pointer moves into its slot and *nb_sd shrinks), walking from the end; the block itself is kept, even when it ends up empty. Entries of other types stay, possibly reordered.
The caller's entry count, read and written with the array (an int, never NULL); C keeps it equal to the number of entry pointers in *sd.

sd is the caller's AVFrameSideData ** variable (never NULL); *sd is NULL with *nb_sd == 0, or an av_realloc_array'd block of *nb_sd pointers to distinct entries, each av_mallocz'd by add_side_data_from_buf_ext and owning its buf reference and metadata dictionary. Drops every entry whose type has a descriptor sharing a bit with props (types without a descriptor stay), as av_frame_side_data_remove does; the block itself is kept.
The caller's entry count, read and written with the array (an int, never NULL); C keeps it equal to the number of entry pointers in *sd.
